question: When was the Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana introduced to provide health insurance to people below the poverty line?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2008**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY) was launched by the Government of India in 2008.
 
• RSBY aims to provide health insurance coverage for Below Poverty Line (BPL) families.
 
• Under this scheme, beneficiaries are entitled to hospitalization coverage up to Rs. 30,000 for most of the diseases that require hospitalization.
 
• The scheme was designed to protect poor families from financial liabilities arising out of health shocks that involve hospitalization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY)**

 
 
• RSBY was introduced by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India.
 
• The scheme provides for cashless insurance for hospital services through an empaneled network of healthcare providers.
 
• Beneficiaries need to pay a registration fee of Rs. 30, and the government pays the premium to the insurer selected by the state government on the basis of a competitive bidding.
 
• The scheme covers all pre-existing conditions and there is no age limit for the beneficiaries.
 
• Transport expenses are also provided to the patient, within an overall limit of Rs. 1000.
 
 
 
• **Health Insurance in India**
 
 
• Health insurance in India is a type of insurance that covers medical expenses incurred by the insured due to health conditions.
 
• Health insurance policies can be purchased by individuals or families to cover a wide range of medical expenses, including hospitalization, surgery, and other medical treatments.
 
• Several government schemes like Ayushman Bharat, PM-JAY, and others aim to provide health insurance coverage to various segments of the population.
 
• The goal of these schemes is to reduce the financial burden of medical expenses and ensure access to quality healthcare services for all.
